answer: Behavioral ridge fingerprinting. Build a per-identity ridge of activity features (inter-request timing, tool-call sequences, error patterns) and score new identities against the population distribution. The signal is divergence from that baseline. Accounts flagged as near-duplicates get throttled pending review. An attacker must vary timing and call structure per clone enough to shift the umber of overlapping features below threshold, which raises their per-identity operational cost.
